takes.speaker: SOLDIER
takes.text: Out of the way! They're coming!

asr.text: Out of the way, they're coming!

takes.speaker: SOLDIER
takes.text: How far are we going?

asr.text: How far are we going?

takes.speaker: BERTHIER
takes.text: Orders to concentrate the corps. Take them.

asr.text: Orders to concentrate the core. Take them.

takes.speaker: BERTHIER
takes.text: No report of their arrival yet. Wait for word.

asr.text: No report of their arrival yet. Wait for word.

takes.speaker: MURAT
takes.text: If we stay scattered, the enemy will take us one by one. Let us ask to withdraw together.

asr.text: If we stay scattered, the enemy will take us one by one. Let us ask to withdraw together.

takes.speaker: SOULT
takes.text: My outposts have been pushed back too.

asr.text: My outposts have been pushed back to.

takes.speaker: SOULT
takes.text: Marshal Lannes, you write it. We are of one mind.

asr.text: Marshall Lannis, you write it. We are of one mind.

takes.speaker: LANNES
takes.text: I shall make clear that you both agree.

asr.text: I shall make clear that you both agree.

takes.speaker: NAPOLEON
takes.text: Soult, what do you think?

asr.text: So, what do you think?

takes.speaker: SOULT
takes.text: Sire, my corps can face twice its number.

asr.text: Sire. My core can face twice its number.

takes.speaker: LANNES
takes.text: You asked me to write it, and now I am the only one asking?

asr.text: You asked me to write it, and now I am the only one asking.

takes.speaker: SOULT
takes.text: He asked about my corps.

asr.text: He asked about my core.

takes.speaker: LANNES
takes.text: Marshal Soult, I challenge you to a duel.

asr.text: Marshall Salt, I challenge you to a duel.

takes.speaker: NAPOLEON
takes.text: We must bring the army together. We shall withdraw.

asr.text: We must bring the army together. We shall withdraw.

takes.speaker: NAPOLEON
takes.text: Move the army back. Send the orders to withdraw.

asr.text: Move the army back. Send the orders to withdraw.

takes.speaker: BERTHIER
takes.text: Yes, Sire.

asr.text: Yes, I am.

takes.speaker: WEYROTHER
takes.text: We go down this way and cut the road. Each column will take its assigned route.

asr.text: We go down this way and cut the road. Each column will take its assigned route.

takes.speaker: STAFF OFFICER
takes.text: Read that part again.

asr.text: Read that part again.

takes.speaker: SOLDIERS
takes.text: Long live the Emperor!

asr.text: Long live the emperor!

takes.speaker: LANNES
takes.text: I sent you a challenge. I thought you knew how to use a sword.

asr.text: I sent you a challenge. I thought you knew how to use a sword.

takes.speaker: SOULT
takes.text: We have more important business today.

asr.text: We have more important business today.

takes.speaker: LANNES
takes.text: You contemptible man.

asr.text: You contemptible man!

takes.speaker: SOLDIER
takes.text: Pass some this way!

asr.text: Pass some this way!

takes.speaker: DAVOUT
takes.text: Put the men who are here into the line. We cannot wait for the rest.

asr.text: Put the men who are here into the line. We cannot wait for the rest.

takes.speaker: NAPOLEON
takes.text: Strike the center. We must take the ground they have left.

asr.text: Strike the center. We must take the ground they have left.

takes.speaker: SOULT
takes.text: Yes, Sire.

asr.text: Yes, I said...

takes.speaker: AUTHOR
takes.text: Our first story stops on the night of victory. The quarrel over the duel comes from an account Thiébault said he heard from Lannes's aide; the Guard cavalry sequence follows Rapp's later memoir within a narrow scope. We reconstructed the conversations and the lives of unnamed soldiers. Please remember that these memoirs are not recordings of that day. Beside tonight's cheering, we have left a place for those who did not return.
